summary: The candidate is a substantial partial fix and passes its regression and the full function-call suite, but Mistral canonical JSON arrays still reproduce the original loss/corruption when valid JSON commas use no whitespace, newline whitespace, or tab whitespace instead of exactly one space.

tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, reproduced Mistral remainder leakage, final-chunk trailing-call loss across six detectors, and coarse JsonArrayParser buffering; on the candidate, confirmed the submitted scenarios pass.
At the exact candidate commit, 256 focused tests and 4 subtests passed.
At the exact candidate commit, 551 function-call tests and 21 subtests passed.

At the exact candidate commit, one-character Mistral canonical-array streams with comma-only, comma-newline, and comma-tab separators lost the trailing valid call and emitted the remainder as normal text; comma-space passed.

gpu_execution_evidence: The changed and exercised paths are deterministic pure-Python incremental parsers; no GPU or model execution is involved.
remaining_counterexamples: Mistral canonical-array streaming of valid JSON with ',' separators returns only the first valid call and exposes the unknown and trailing valid calls as normal text.
The same Mistral failure occurs with valid JSON whitespace separators ',\n' and ',\t'; the candidate only handles the literal ', '.
Hermes coarse/whole batches containing an unknown call add an extra closing tool tag to normal text compared with the equivalent valid-only batch.
remaining_limitations: No model weights, HTTP serving path, semantic model behavior, GPU execution, or distributed workload was tested or claimed.
No native code changed and the prepared environment declares no native component, so no native rebuild was applicable.
